clue.text: Greek character holds a lively dance

indicators.note: the Greek letter holds the next piece inside it, as a container wraps its contents

parts.note: lambda is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person is gripping a partner during an energetic dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts A inside LAMBDA, between the B and the D.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a fast, sensual Brazilian partner dance, so it is a lively dance by example.

clue.text: It's used in Tripoli by a native

definitions.text: It's used in Tripoli by a native

indicators.note: the answer is used in, that is sits within, the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A word that someone from Tripoli would use.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'tripoLI BY A Native'; the whole clue doubles as the definition, since Tripoli is the capital of Libya.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the Libyan capital, so a native found there is someone from Libya.

clue.text: Like a less attractive dog, one denying access to others?

definitions.meaning: a mangy dog is scruffy with mange
a dog in the manger keeps others from what it cannot use; read as 'I (one) in MANGER' it spells the letters

explanation.surface: A scruffy dog guards something it will not share.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a pun: the proverbial dog in the manger denies others access, and putting I (one) into MANGER gives the answer's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mange is a skin disease that makes a dog scruffy, so the comparative describes a shabbier animal.

clue.text: Parent entering reform school

indicators.note: the parent word goes into the reform word, like someone entering a building

parts.note: to reform something is to alter it
mama is a child's word for a mother, a parent

explanation.surface: A mother or father is going into a reform school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' looks like it describes the school, but it is a verb giving the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: One's alma mater is the school or university one attended.

clue.text: Go after the rats? A bar member's put fellows inside

indicators.note: the fellows are put inside the bar-plus-member pair, splitting it in two

parts.note: to bar something is to ban it
a hip is a member, a part of the body; the 's is 'has'
dons are university fellows

explanation.surface: Someone at a bar has invited some companions in.
explanation.walkthrough: Rats are said to desert a sinking ship, so leaving after them is what this order commands.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoning ship means leaving a sinking vessel, which rats famously do first.

clue.text: What constituencies have to charge?

definitions.meaning: each constituency elects one MP, so read as '1 MP each' the letters appear
to charge an official formally with misconduct

explanation.surface: A question about what voters' districts are entitled to bring against someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first definition as I (one) MP EACH: every constituency has one Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach is to bring a formal accusation of wrongdoing against a public official.

clue.text: Characters following every part of her conditions

parts.words: Characters following every part of her
parts.note: take the letter that follows each letter of the word her in the alphabet: H gives I, E gives F, R gives S

explanation.surface: Letters coming after each piece of a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Each letter of HER is moved one step on in the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ifs are provisos or stipulations, as in 'no ifs or buts'.

clue.text: Italian fare supplement produces irritation, nothing more

indicators.note: nothing is added as one more piece after the first

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance, an irritation
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A food additive from Italy causes annoyance and nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more' signals that O is added after PEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is a basil sauce added to Italian pasta dishes, a supplement to the food.

clue.text: Not for profit, in a way

indicators.note: the profit word goes in between the a and the way

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: A non-profit organisation, in some sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not for profit' looks like one phrase, but 'Not for' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Against is the opposite of in favour of, so it means not supporting a cause.

clue.text: Measure introduced by firm to last in business?

definitions.text: Measure introduced by firm to last in business?

indicators.note: the measure comes after, so the earlier pieces introduce it

parts.note: hard means firm

indicators.note: only the final letter of the business word is taken

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: A policy a company adopts to survive commercially.
explanation.walkthrough: HARD and S (the last letter of 'business') introduce ELL; the whole clue also describes the aggressive sales tactic.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard sell is a pushy sales technique, a measure a company might use to stay in trade.

clue.text: Averages close to number initially produced? Not at all!

indicators.note: these pieces are brought out first, before the averages

parts.note: by means near, as in 'stand by me'
means are averages

explanation.surface: Statistics near a figure appear at first, then a cry of denial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially produced' says the close-to and number pieces come out first, ahead of the averages.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic refusal, equivalent to 'certainly not'.

clue.text: Street song that can lift one a little

definitions.text: that can lift one a little

parts.note: an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: A tune from the street can raise someone's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a lifting tune, but it means a step that raises one a short way.
explanation.definitionFit: Each step of a staircase raises a climber a short height.

clue.text: Man installed after a vote, in principle

indicators.note: the Man piece is placed after the vote

parts.note: X is the mark made on a ballot paper
IOM stands for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man takes office after an election, in theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man, IOM.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a self-evident truth taken as a starting point, a basic principle.

clue.text: One's dimes converted into capital in Us

indicators.note: the coins are converted, changed into another form, so their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone's ten-cent coins are changed into American money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges ONES DIMES; 'into' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Des Moines is the state capital of Iowa in the United States.

clue.text: Struck before, splitting layers into fragments

parts.note: smit is an old past tense of smite, to strike

indicators.note: the before word splits the layers word in two by going inside it

parts.note: hens are egg layers
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone hit something first, breaking strata into bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layers' looks geological but means egg-laying birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Smithereens are tiny broken pieces, as in 'smashed to smithereens'.

clue.text: Alloy in yacht used by Bond's superiors

parts.note: Britannia was the British royal yacht
M is James Bond's boss in the spy novels
et al. means 'and others', making M and others superiors in the plural

explanation.surface: A metal used in a boat that James Bond's bosses sail on.
explanation.walkthrough: Britannia was the Royal Yacht, decommissioned in 1997; M plus ET AL gives several superiors.
explanation.definitionFit: Britannia metal is a pewter-like tin alloy with antimony and copper.

clue.text: Infantry officer, for example, encountered carrying second flag

indicators.note: the encountered word carries the others inside it

parts.note: met means encountered
a mo is a moment, a second
the iris, also called flag, is a plant

explanation.surface: A soldier met someone holding a second banner.
explanation.walkthrough: Siegfried Sassoon wrote 'Memoirs of an Infantry Officer', so such an officer exemplifies the answer. 'flag' is the plant, not a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassoon's narrator in 'Memoirs of an Infantry Officer' tells his own life story, the work of a writer of reminiscences.

clue.text: Gentleman on horse who's rewarded with silver?

parts.note: a runner is a horse taking part in a race
in racing a rider mounted is said to be up, as in 'Mr Smith up'

explanation.surface: A mounted gentleman who wins a silver trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: Racecards name the jockey with 'up' after the name, as in 'Mr Smith up', so the gentleman goes after the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Second place earns a silver medal, so the competitor finishing second gets silver.

clue.text: Where a key is being auctioned

definitions.meaning: a piano key sits beneath the hammer that strikes the string
on sale at an auction, where the gavel falls

explanation.surface: A piano key is up for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: In a piano each key lifts a felt hammer, so the key is beneath it; an auctioneer's gavel is also called a hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: Auction lots are sold when the auctioneer's gavel falls, so goods on sale are said to be beneath it.

clue.text: Old woman's encouragement to take a chance

parts.note: 'Do!' is an urging imperative, encouragement to act
to wager is to bet, to take a chance

explanation.surface: A grandmother urges someone to have a flutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do wager!' is the encouragement; the 's of the definition is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow holding a title from her late husband, typically an elderly lady.

clue.text: Free-lance vet wasting little time in isolated country area

indicators.note: the letters are set free from their order and rearranged

parts.note: T is short for time

explanation.surface: A freelance vet loses time working in a remote rural district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasting' drops T from LANCE VET, and 'Free' rearranges the remaining LANCEVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclave is a territory wholly surrounded by another, so it is cut off from its neighbours.

clue.text: Playwright boosted by uplifting atmosphere in house

indicators.note: the turned atmosphere goes in the playwright's name

parts.note: Christopher Fry was an English playwright

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting the word up reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: air is the atmosphere

explanation.surface: A dramatist is cheered by a positive mood at home.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'uplifting' reads the atmosphere from bottom to top, giving RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A friary is a religious house where friars live.

clue.text: Publication of novel, perhaps, not hard to arrange

parts.note: new means novel

indicators.note: the remaining letters are set out in a new arrangement

parts.note: H is short for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Bringing out a book, perhaps, isn't difficult to organise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but means NEW; 'not' removes H from PERHAPS, and 'to arrange' reorders PERAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper is a periodical publication of news.

clue.text: Like a future monarch, perhaps — one instructed soundly

indicators.note: the word is heard rather than read, so its sound gives the letters

parts.note: a pupil is one who is taught

explanation.surface: A future king, perhaps, was well taught.
explanation.walkthrough: A monarch is a butterfly, so a future one is a pupa, not a crown prince.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch butterfly passes through a pupa stage, so its developing form is pupa-like.

clue.text: I see you are, so to speak, pinching North's contract

indicators.note: the spoken letters pinch, holding the north letter between them
the phrase is said aloud as letter names

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like ICUR
N is short for north

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on a person stealing a northern agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I see you are' said aloud is I C U R; N goes after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract a debt or illness is to bring it on oneself, to incur it.

clue.text: Improvise telephone with no end of invention

indicators.note: the next piece is taken away from the telephone word

parts.note: to ring up is to telephone

indicators.note: only the final letter of invention is used

explanation.surface: Make do with a phone call without a finished invention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of invention' removes N, the last letter of 'invention'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rig up is to put together a makeshift arrangement, to improvise one.

clue.text: Continental artefacts found in steamer I can authenticate

indicators.note: the answer is found in the run of words, spanning them

explanation.surface: Someone vouches for antiques discovered aboard a steamship.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through 'steAMER I CAN Authenticate'; Continental here means of the American continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Americana are objects typical of American culture and history.

clue.text: Fourth of March issue — vast number run off

indicators.note: the run letter goes off, removed from the vast number

parts.note: an army is a vast number, as in an army of ants
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: The fourth issue of a March magazine had a huge print run cut.
explanation.walkthrough: March here is the family in 'Little Women', whose youngest daughter, the fourth, is Amy; 'issue' means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'Little Women' the March sisters are Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy, the youngest child.

clue.text: Herb's son is intermediary in negotiations

indicators.note: the son sits in the middle of the negotiations, between parties

parts.note: a parley is a negotiation between enemies

explanation.surface: A man's boy acts as go-between in talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' looks like a man's name but is the plant; S goes inside PARLEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsley is a culinary herb with curled or flat leaves.

clue.text: Gratification as composer finishes off Schubert symphony

parts.note: Erik Satie was a French composer

indicators.note: only the final letters of the two following words are taken

explanation.surface: Pleasure as one composer completes another's unfinished symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: Schubert's 'Unfinished' symphony makes the surface plausible; T and Y are the last letters of 'Schubert' and 'symphony'.
explanation.definitionFit: Satiety is the state of being fully satisfied, gratification to the point of fullness.
